parameters.content:
## Speed-to-Lead Automation Workflow

Starter template from agentmelt.com — configure before running:

1. Fill in "Config (edit me)" (name, approver, quiet hours; test_mode stays on for the first week).
2. Add credentials to every service node (Anthropic, mail, CRM, database…).
3. Replace placeholder URLs, queries and field mappings with yours.
4. Set the trigger: A lead email from Zillow or Realtor.com, a website form submission, or a new-person webhook from Follow Up Boss or kvCORE starts the run.
5. Keep the gates: 'Needs a person?' after every AI step, 'Approved?' after the approval — wire their dead ends to a sheet or a channel.
6. Keep the guardrails:
   - Quiet hours: nothing sent 9 pm–8 am in the lead's time zone; messages queue until morning.
   - One question per message; the second message asks the next question, never both at once.
   - SMS only with a number the lead gave on a form; STOP honoured on the first word and written to the CRM.
   - Fair-housing language check on every draft; flagged drafts cannot be sent.
   - Approval mode for the first week: drafts go to the agent for a tap before sending.

Full blueprint and pricing: https://agentmelt.com/workflows/speed-to-lead-automation/
Want it built and run for you? $197/month · custom $2,000–3,500 one-time

nodes.name: Webhook: Receive the lead
nodes.notes:
Receive the lead

Name, email, phone, source, the property or page they enquired from, and their message. Portal emails are parsed for the same fields.

assignments.name: config.your_name
assignments.value: Your name — signs every outgoing message

assignments.name: config.approver
assignments.value: #approvals — a Slack channel, or an email address

nodes.name: Config (edit me)
nodes.notes:
Fill these in once; every later node reads them as $('Config (edit me)').item.json.config.*

test_mode = true: log what the workflow would write, without writing it, for the first week.
approval_mode = true: the approval node waits for a person; switch off per message type once it has earned it.

Also point the nodes at your own sources:
- Portal lead emails or site form
- CRM (Follow Up Boss, kvCORE, HubSpot)
- Agent voice samples
- Calendar for showing slots
- Consent and opt-out records

options.systemMessage:
You are the "Qualify" step of the Speed-to-Lead Automation Workflow workflow run by Agentmelt.
Task: Timeline, pre-approval, price band and intent from the enquiry text; 'hot' only when the timeline is near and something specific is named. Nothing is inferred beyond the text.

Rules:
- Quiet hours: nothing sent 9 pm–8 am in the lead's time zone; messages queue until morning.
- One question per message; the second message asks the next question, never both at once.
- SMS only with a number the lead gave on a form; STOP honoured on the first word and written to the CRM.
- Fair-housing language check on every draft; flagged drafts cannot be sent.
- Approval mode for the first week: drafts go to the agent for a tap before sending.
- Answer only from the data provided in the input. If something is missing, say so in the output instead of guessing.
- If this step produces a message or a document, put the full text in `draft` (and a `subject` if it is an email); put a one-line summary in `summary`.
- Set `needs_human` true whenever you are unsure, the input is unusual, or a rule above applies; a person will look at it.
- Return valid JSON matching the output schema; no prose outside the JSON.

Check quiet hours and consent

Holds the message until quiet hours end in the lead's time zone; checks that a phone number came with consent before any SMS; skips leads who opted out.

nodes.name: Wait: Follow up on silence
nodes.notes:
Follow up on silence

Two days without a reply: one nudge that offers two showing slots or asks what they are after. A reply at any point stops everything and forwards the thread to the agent.
